Title: AP sub-ledger vs GL reconciliation difference is non-zero (data integrity check)
Preconditions: AP transactions seeded and posted in system
Expected: difference should be 0 per BR-AP-02; GL 2100 credit balance should equal AP sub-ledger outstanding
Actual: HTTP 200; subLedgerTotal=940633.7, glControlBalance=-1045055.54, difference=1985689.24. GL 2100 trial-balance net=+1045055.54 (debit > credit, unusual for a liability), negated to -1045055.54. Difference is not 0.
Defect: AP reconciliation difference=1985689.24 (should be 0). The GL 2100 Accounts Payable control account shows a net debit balance (DR 38890109 > CR 37845053.46), which is inverted for a liability. Either (a) the seeded AP payments incorrectly DR AP more than they CR it, (b) the reconciliation query computes the GL period without date bounds while sub-ledger totals all open bills (period mismatch), or (c) bills were posted to GL at different amounts than entered. Finance-grade defect per NFR-AP-01. Suggested owner: backend-engineer agent to check ApReconciliationQuery vs TrialBalanceQuery date scoping.

Title: versionStatus filter parameter accepted but silently ignored - no filtering occurs
Preconditions: 11 total budgets for companyId=1 with various version statuses

Title: Approve second version should supersede prior APPROVED version in same TX
Preconditions: Budget 11 has v1 APPROVED. v3 in SUBMITTED status with lines. Same companyId/fiscalYear/costCentre scope.
Steps: 1) Verify v1 status=APPROVED, 2) POST approve on v3 (expect v1 moves to SUPERSEDED), 3) Verify v1 is now SUPERSEDED
Expected: HTTP 200, v3 becomes APPROVED, v1 becomes SUPERSEDED (in same TX via PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)
Actual: HTTP 409; errors=["A record with the same unique identifier already exists."] - repeated 3 times. v1 remains APPROVED. v3 stuck in SUBMITTED. DB partial unique index uq_budget_version_one_approved_companywide fires before the supersede save is committed.
Defect: Supersede-on-approve is broken: approving a new version when a prior APPROVED version exists for the same company/FY/null-costCentre scope throws a DB unique constraint violation instead of atomically superseding the prior. The partial unique index uq_budget_version_one_approved_companywide prevents two APPROVED rows. The service sets prior.status=SUPERSEDED and saves, then sets new.status=APPROVED and saves, but JPA may not flush the first save before the constraint check on commit. Fix: add an explicit entityManager.flush() or use a JPQL UPDATE for the supersede to guarantee order of DB writes before the new APPROVED insert/update.

Title: Recalculate payroll from CALCULATED/APPROVED status - fails with 409 (bug)
Preconditions: Payroll run in CALCULATED or APPROVED status (lines already exist)
Steps: 1) POST calculate on run in DRAFT to get CALCULATED 2) POST calculate again (from CALCULATED) - expect idempotent recalculation
Test_Data: uid=01KVMC42R8W2BXK00V3T65J475 (July 2026 run, APPROVED after first calculate)
Expected: HTTP 200, lines deleted and recalculated (service code at line 193 promises idempotency for DRAFT/CALCULATED/APPROVED)
Actual: HTTP 409; errors=["A record with the same unique identifier already exists."] — service fails on second calculate; existing lines not properly flushed before new inserts violate uq_payroll_line_run_employee constraint
Defect: PayrollRunServiceImpl.calculate() purports to be idempotent (delete existing lines, re-insert) but triggers a DB unique-constraint violation (uq_payroll_line_run_employee) on any re-run. The Hibernate session does not flush the delete before the insert within the same transaction, leaving the constraint in a violated state. Affects any re-calculate from CALCULATED or APPROVED status. Fix: add EntityManager.flush() after deleteAll() calls, or use a native DELETE statement before reinsert.

Title: PUT preference with empty JSON body {} silently creates preference with muted=false and channelsEnabled=null
Preconditions: Authenticated; no preference exists for INVOICE_OVERDUE
Expected: HTTP 400 (validation error - required fields missing) or explicit default documentation
Actual: HTTP 200; data={muted:false, channelsEnabled:null} created silently - empty body accepted with primitive defaults
Defect: SetPreferenceRequest accepts empty {} body: muted (primitive boolean) defaults to false, channelsEnabled (String) defaults to null. A user who accidentally sends an empty body gets a preference created with null channelsEnabled, which is a valid state but may suppress all channel notifications without intent. Same root cause as NOTIFICATIONS-017: Java record with primitive boolean + nullable String fields and no @NotNull/@NotBlank constraints. Low severity since it requires authentication and only affects the user's own preferences.

Title: PUT preference with non-existent typeKey silently creates orphan preference row
Preconditions: Authenticated; typeKey DOES_NOT_EXIST_TYPE has no corresponding notification_type row
Steps: 1) Login. 2) PUT /api/v1/notification-preferences/DOES_NOT_EXIST_TYPE with {muted:false, channelsEnabled:'IN_APP'}. 3) GET list to confirm it appears.
Expected: HTTP 404 (typeKey does not reference a known notification type) or HTTP 400
Actual: HTTP 200; orphan preference created: id='3', typeKey='DOES_NOT_EXIST_TYPE'. GET list returns 3 records including this orphan. No FK validation on typeKey.
Defect: NotificationPreferenceServiceImpl.setPreference() performs no existence check against notification_types for the given typeKey. A caller can persist preferences for arbitrary typeKey strings that have no matching type catalogue entry. These orphan rows will appear in the list endpoint and confuse the UI (no display name, no template). There is no DB FK constraint enforcing the reference either. Fix: validate that the typeKey exists in notification_types for the caller's company before creating the preference, returning 404/422 if not found.

Fix: add server.error.include-stacktrace=never to application.yml (or at minimum application-prod.yml). Also affects /api/v1/trial-balance (wrong path), /api/v1/stock (wrong subpath), /api/v1/chart-of-accounts, and any mistyped /api/** URL.

Preconditions: Two active blankets in same company (01KVE0M1ZVRHMC3WD115V2PP68 and 01KVE0M1W5ZZ6ECPDEFF1AGVZD)

Actual: HTTP 200; draw succeeded against BLANKET_B using BLANKET_A's path-uid for permission check — @PreAuthorize uses path uid only for scope check, actual operation targets body blanketUid
Defect: BlanketOrderController.draw() uses #uid (path param) for @PreAuthorize scope check but then calls blanketOrderService.drawAgainstBlanket(request) which uses request.blanketUid() from the body. At minimum the controller should assert path uid == body blanketUid before delegating, or the path uid should not be used at all (use body uid for both permission and operation).
